senses.exampleSentence: Oil prices fluctuated throughout the year.

senses.englishDefinition: To stay the same.
senses.exampleSentence: The figure remained stable at around 20 per cent.

senses.englishDefinition: To reach the highest point.
senses.exampleSentence: Sales peaked in December.

senses.englishDefinition: To stop rising and stay at a steady level.
senses.exampleSentence: The number of users plateaued after 2018.

senses.englishDefinition: A small and short fall in a level or amount.
senses.exampleSentence: There was a slight dip in March.

senses.englishDefinition: A sudden and large increase.
senses.exampleSentence: The report shows a surge in online shopping.

senses.englishDefinition: A gradual fall in number, quality or strength.
senses.exampleSentence: The decline in newspaper sales continued.

senses.englishDefinition: To rise quickly to a very high level.
senses.exampleSentence: House prices soared during the 2000s.

senses.englishDefinition: To fall suddenly and by a large amount.
senses.exampleSentence: Profits plummeted after the factory closed.

senses.englishDefinition: Slowly and by small amounts.
senses.exampleSentence: The temperature gradually increased.

senses.englishDefinition: Suddenly and by a large amount.
senses.exampleSentence: Exports fell sharply in 2009.

senses.englishDefinition: At a regular and continuous rate.
senses.exampleSentence: The population has grown steadily since 1950.

senses.englishDefinition: A part of a whole.
senses.exampleSentence: A large proportion of the budget is spent on health.

senses.englishDefinition: An amount expressed as a part of one hundred.
senses.exampleSentence: The percentage of women in the workforce has risen.

senses.englishDefinition: A number, especially in official statistics.
senses.exampleSentence: The latest figures show a fall in crime.

senses.englishDefinition: A person who is important or well known.
senses.exampleSentence: He is a respected figure in the film industry.

senses.englishDefinition: A general direction in which something is changing.
senses.exampleSentence: The graph shows a clear upward trend.

senses.englishDefinition: Taking everything into account.
senses.exampleSentence: Overall, the number of students increased.

senses.englishDefinition: About, not exactly.
senses.exampleSentence: Approximately 60 per cent of people agreed.

senses.englishDefinition: The larger part of a group.
senses.exampleSentence: The majority of respondents prefer public transport.

senses.englishDefinition: To become twice as large.
senses.exampleSentence: The number of cars doubled in ten years.

senses.englishDefinition: To form a particular part or amount of something.
senses.exampleSentence: Housing accounts for 30 per cent of spending.

senses.englishDefinition: In the order mentioned.
senses.exampleSentence: Sales in 2019 and 2020 were 5 and 8 million respectively.

senses.englishDefinition: By a large and noticeable amount.
senses.exampleSentence: Costs fell significantly after the change.

senses.englishDefinition: In a sudden and very noticeable way.
senses.exampleSentence: Energy use dropped dramatically in summer.

senses.englishDefinition: By a small amount.
senses.exampleSentence: The price rose slightly in April.

senses.englishDefinition: The relationship between two amounts, shown as a pair of numbers.
senses.exampleSentence: The ratio of teachers to students is one to twenty.

senses.englishDefinition: To give reasons to support an opinion.
senses.exampleSentence: Some experts argue that homework is unnecessary.

senses.englishDefinition: To publicly support an idea or plan.
senses.exampleSentence: Doctors advocate regular exercise.

senses.englishDefinition: To state something firmly as true.
senses.exampleSentence: He asserted that the policy had failed.

senses.englishDefinition: To say that something is true without proof.
senses.exampleSentence: Critics claim that the tax is unfair.

senses.englishDefinition: To suggest something without saying it directly.
senses.exampleSentence: The results imply that diet affects mood.

senses.englishDefinition: To show the meaning of something by examples.
senses.exampleSentence: The chart illustrates changes in population.

senses.englishDefinition: To give special importance to something.
senses.exampleSentence: The teacher emphasised the need for practice.

senses.englishDefinition: A result of an action or situation.
senses.exampleSentence: Obesity is a consequence of poor diet and inactivity.

senses.englishDefinition: Something that helps you to be better or more successful.
senses.exampleSentence: One advantage of online learning is flexibility.

senses.englishDefinition: Something that makes a situation worse.
senses.exampleSentence: A major disadvantage is the high cost.

senses.englishDefinition: A helpful or good effect.
senses.exampleSentence: Exercise has many health benefits.

senses.englishDefinition: A disadvantage or problem.
senses.exampleSentence: The main drawback of the plan is its cost.

senses.englishDefinition: Absolutely necessary.
senses.exampleSentence: Clean water is essential for life.

senses.englishDefinition: Forming the base or most important part.
senses.exampleSentence: Respect is fundamental to any relationship.

senses.englishDefinition: Causing public disagreement.
senses.exampleSentence: Animal testing is a controversial subject.

senses.englishDefinition: A strong effect on something.
senses.exampleSentence: Social media has a big impact on young people.

senses.englishDefinition: One of several things that influence a result.
senses.exampleSentence: Cost is a key factor when choosing a university.

senses.englishDefinition: An important topic that people discuss.
senses.exampleSentence: Traffic congestion is a major issue in big cities.

senses.englishDefinition: To be likely to do something or to happen often.
senses.exampleSentence: Young people tend to spend more time online.

senses.englishDefinition: To accept that something is true without checking.
senses.exampleSentence: People often assume that expensive means better.

senses.englishDefinition: To accept that something is true or exists.
senses.exampleSentence: We must acknowledge the risks of the plan.

senses.englishDefinition: To keep something at the same level, or to state an opinion firmly.
senses.exampleSentence: She maintains that school uniforms are unnecessary.

senses.englishDefinition: A clear difference between two things.
senses.exampleSentence: There is a sharp contrast between city and village life.

senses.englishDefinition: Also, and more importantly.
senses.exampleSentence: The plan is cheap; moreover, it is quick to carry out.

senses.englishDefinition: In spite of that.
senses.exampleSentence: The test was hard; nevertheless, most students passed.

senses.englishDefinition: Used to compare two different things.
senses.exampleSentence: Cities are crowded, whereas villages are quiet.

senses.englishDefinition: For that reason.
senses.exampleSentence: Prices are rising; therefore, many people save less.

senses.englishDefinition: As a result.
senses.exampleSentence: The factory closed; consequently, many workers lost their jobs.

senses.englishDefinition: In spite of the fact that.
senses.exampleSentence: Although it was expensive, the course was worth it.

senses.englishDefinition: In the same way.
senses.exampleSentence: Parents should be role models; likewise, teachers should set an example.

senses.englishDefinition: The business of providing services for people who travel for pleasure.
senses.exampleSentence: Tourism is the main source of income for the island.

senses.englishDefinition: The place where someone or something is going.
senses.exampleSentence: Da Nang is a popular holiday destination.

senses.englishDefinition: A place to live or stay.
senses.exampleSentence: Student accommodation is cheap near the campus.

senses.englishDefinition: A detailed plan of a journey.
senses.exampleSentence: Our itinerary includes three cities in five days.

senses.englishDefinition: An official document that you need to travel abroad.
senses.exampleSentence: You must show your passport at the border.

senses.englishDefinition: An act of travelling from one place to another.
senses.exampleSentence: The journey from Hanoi to Hue takes about an hour by plane.

senses.englishDefinition: A building or place that is easy to recognise.
senses.exampleSentence: The tower is the best-known landmark in the city.

senses.englishDefinition: A place that people visit for interest or enjoyment.
senses.exampleSentence: The museum is a major tourist attraction.

senses.englishDefinition: The basic systems of a country, such as roads and electricity.
senses.exampleSentence: Good infrastructure attracts foreign investment.

senses.englishDefinition: A situation in which a place is too crowded, especially with traffic.
senses.exampleSentence: Traffic congestion wastes time and fuel.

senses.englishDefinition: A person who walks rather than travels in a vehicle.
senses.exampleSentence: The new bridge is for pedestrians only.

senses.englishDefinition: Buses, trains and other services that anyone can use.
senses.exampleSentence: Public transport is cheaper than owning a car.

senses.englishDefinition: A notice that tries to persuade people to buy something.
senses.exampleSentence: The advertisement for the phone appeared everywhere.

senses.englishDefinition: A programme on television or radio.
senses.exampleSentence: The live broadcast attracted millions of viewers.

senses.englishDefinition: A person who writes news reports for newspapers or television.
senses.exampleSentence: The journalist interviewed the mayor.

senses.englishDefinition: A famous person.
senses.exampleSentence: Celebrities often influence what young people buy.

senses.englishDefinition: Films, music and other things that people enjoy watching.
senses.exampleSentence: Home entertainment has changed with streaming.

senses.englishDefinition: A film that gives facts about a real subject.
senses.exampleSentence: The documentary explains how glaciers are melting.

senses.englishDefinition: A public show of art or other objects.
senses.exampleSentence: The exhibition features paintings from the last century.

senses.englishDefinition: A special event or celebration, often held every year.
senses.exampleSentence: The lantern festival attracts visitors from abroad.

senses.englishDefinition: A building where important objects are kept and shown.
senses.exampleSentence: Entry to the national museum is free on Sundays.

senses.englishDefinition: A style of cooking.
senses.exampleSentence: Vietnamese cuisine is famous for fresh herbs.
